Hi Sara — thanks, this is great context. I pulled a compact breakdown (see attached SKU matrix) that shows three pricing paths: seat-first HSM, usage-first KMS, and a blended reserved+overflow. High level: 

- HSM (seat model): base monthly per-seat + optional managed-service fee. Seats include up to 1M signing ops/month; overflow billed at $0.00X per 1000.
- KMS (usage model): reserved commit option (monthly commit covers N requests) + per-10k overflow. This is typically ~25–40% cheaper at high volume vs pure seat if you have spiky peaks.
- Hybrid/blend: reserve a small # of HSM seats for low-latency, high-security keys + KMS for ephemeral keys/less-sensitive traffic.

I've proposed two discount schedules in the matrix: commit-tier discounts (3 levels) and term-based credits (12/24/36mo). There's also a HIPAA residency uplift (listed as a % lift when EU-only).

Sara / Rachel — quick clarifications on HSM pricing: 

- Our standard seat includes 1M signing ops/month; overflow = $3.50 per 10k signing ops.
- Managed HSM service fee covers patching, key rotation automation, and quarterly attestations — $1,200/seat/month (negotiable with term).
- EU-only physical HSM pool: we can provision but there is a one-time setup of $25k and a monthly regional isolation fee (~15% uplift) due to dedicated hardware and network egress controls.

If MediTex expects primarily steady-state traffic >5M signing ops/mo, the usage-blend with a medium commit is usually the most cost-effective. If latency and strict FIPS/HSM certs are non-negotiable for PHI flows, seats make sense for that subset.
